newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House passes bill to fight telemarketing fraud.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House passes bill to fight telemarketing fraud.

text.p: The House passed legislation Tuesday to crack down on telemarketing fraud that robs consumers of some $40 billion annually.

The bill, which passed on a voice vote, would lengthen federal prison terms for telemarketing crimes and give prosecutors more tools through conspiracy laws to find masterminds behind big "boiler room" operations, bill sponsor Rep. Bob Goodlatte, a Virginia Republican, said.
The bill calls for much harsher sentences for criminals who prey on the elderly, who comprise a disproportionate share of the victims.
It also would sharply lengthen sentences for those who shift criminal operations overseas to try to avoid prosecution.
The bill also requires that equipment used in telemarketing fraud crimes be forfeited to ensure it is not used for such crimes again.

Americans lose at least $40 billion a year to telemarketing fraud, according to the National Consumers League. Older people who tend to be more polite and curious are the most vulnerable targets, it said.

"This legislation is a vital step toward combating the unscrupulous telemarketers who prey on our nation's elderly. It is incumbent upon Congress to protect Americans from criminals who steal not only money, but dignity, self-confidence and pride," Florida Republican Bill McCollum, who chairs a House Judiciary subcommittee on crime, said.
Arizona Republican John Kyl is pushing a similar bill in the Senate.
